modules.docstring: Task-execution primitives separated from ordinary character chat.

Restricted DOCX text import and simple Markdown-to-Word export.

DOCX is a ZIP/XML container and is treated as untrusted input. Import is
deliberately text-only: unsupported parts or constructs are rejected instead
of silently producing an incomplete representation that could be mistaken
for a faithful edit of the original document.
MCP action policy for the three user-selected task permission tiers.

Built-in, task-scoped workspace tools.

These tools never edit user-selected originals. Drafts are written to the
task's deliverables directory with exclusive-create semantics.
First-party Windows UI Automation MCP, started only as an STDIO child.
HTTP surface for task workspaces and their durable event stream.
Chat-facing turn protocol. HTTP/SSE clients do not own execution lifetime.
User-triggered short-recording speech-to-text endpoints.

User-created character drafts (ADR 0018): compile a structured draft
into a plain CharacterSkill folder. Zero dedicated runtime logic — after
save, the character is an ordinary skill like any imported one. AI
generation (preview samples / draft completion) uses the single language
slot and only runs inside these user-triggered endpoints.

User data management endpoints (ADR 0027).

GET  /settings/data/inventory  — three-state inventory (display only)
POST /settings/data/delete     — explicit per-category deletion; the
service layer re-verifies every dependency at execution time.

There is no scheduled or automatic deletion anywhere behind these
endpoints; UNKNOWN items are never removed and partial failures come
back as 200 + ``status: "partial"`` with per-item details.

Desktop-pet API — state, image pack, AI generation, settings, react.

Serves the second (transparent, always-on-top) window and the settings
tab in the main UI. Reuses existing engines:

- active character: ``desktop_session_store`` (fallback:
  ``settings.wx_default_character`` → first available skill)
- emotion: ``EmotionEngine.current_emotion`` (branch-scoped)
- relationship stage: ``RelationshipEngine.get_state().stage``
- proactive bubbles: the pet page subscribes to the existing
  ``GET /chat/events`` SSE channel — no new push path needed.
- TTS: the pet page calls the existing ``/voice/preview``.

AI generation (``POST /pet/generate`` and the portrait job runner) uses
GPT Image 2.5 (``backend/capabilities/openai_image_generation.py``) with the
canonical reference attached, so emotion variants keep the same character's
look.  Generated images always stage as review-gated candidates, never
written straight into the live pack.

Step 4 — /pet/outbox + ack + result endpoints.

The Electron host (and PetApp) reads commands via these. SSE delivery
is added in Step 6 / later — for now PetApp uses long-poll + ack.

Proactive-messaging operator endpoints.

Only a manual test hook right now — bypasses the trigger judgment and fires
one proactive message immediately so the full generate→persist→SSE-push
chain can be verified without waiting for a trigger to come due.

Provider settings API: model providers, model catalog, discovery and
the ``chat.primary`` binding (ADR 0014; single language slot per ADR 0015).

Design notes:

* Endpoints live under ``/settings``.  The old model endpoints remain only as
  deprecated adapters for existing scripts; the UI and all new code use the
  binding below.
  Since ADR 0015 the ``chat.primary`` binding IS the single language slot:
  saving it writes through to the legacy ``settings.primary_model`` /
  ``settings.llm_provider`` caches so every text-generation caller follows
  the same model.  ``GET/POST /settings/model`` remain narrow legacy aliases
  (the UI no longer exposes them).
* Responses never contain credential values — only ``has_key`` / source
  style status.  Secrets are accepted on write and forwarded to the
  existing api_key_store-backed storage.
* Model discovery is a user-triggered convenience: it never runs at
  startup or in tests/CI, never writes anything, and a failed discovery
  is reported as a soft error — it does NOT mean the provider is broken
  and manual model entry always remains available.
* Deleting a model/provider that ``chat.primary`` still references
  returns 409 instead of silently rebinding the user to another
  (potentially paid) provider.

Skill auto-adaptation endpoint. Analyzes markdown skill files via LLM
and generates keyword headers for on-demand module injection.

Theme asset persistence — background image + per‑character avatars.

Background images are persisted to ``data/theme/background.<ext>`` so a
page reload sees the same image. The frontend stores only a URL path in
localStorage (~50 bytes), not the multi‑MB base64 string.

Avatars follow the same pattern under ``data/theme/avatars/<character>.<ext>``.

Image upload + serving. User-attached images (paste / drag-drop) are uploaded here BEFORE the chat request, so the chat interface can carry lightweight URL references instead of fat base64 strings through every hop. Files are persisted to ``data/uploads//.`` so they survive page reloads and device changes, and the URLs they return can be embedded in ``Message.images`` for long-term display. The ``/api/uploads/serve`` route is a plain static-style file response mounted in ``main.py`` (with branch-id scoping at the URL level), so the frontend can ```` straight off disk.

Voice management API — clone, list, assign, preview, delete.

All MiniMax-dependent endpoints degrade gracefully when the API is
unreachable (e.g. no balance): they return a descriptive error field
instead of a 500 so the frontend can show a user-friendly message.

WeChat iLink bot debug + control endpoints.

These are operator-facing, not user-facing. They let the desktop shell's
Settings dialog inspect / disable / restart the iLink bot without a
process restart.

Single-user model (post-A3): the bot has at most one bound owner_openid,
and WeChat reuses the desktop session's currently-published
``(character, branch_id)`` for chat routing. The per-openid branch /
character / session endpoints that used to live here are gone.

Default-disabled in ``config.settings.wx_bot_enabled`` — even with the
endpoints mounted, the bot stays dormant when ``wx_bot_enabled`` is
``False`` (the ``/wx/status`` endpoint surfaces that).

Capability plugin framework.

A *capability* is an opt-in backend-side ability that augments a chat turn
without exposing itself as an LLM tool. The user triggers the capability
explicitly via the UI (a toggle / upload button), and the result is injected
into the system prompt as plain context. The model never knows it has a
"tool" — it just sees extra information.

This is the philosophy we deliberately picked over function-calling:

* it matches ai-companion's branch-scoped, markdown-first skill model
* the user owns the trigger, not the model (no surprise tool calls)
* capability outputs (e.g. search snippets) never enter long-term memory
  unless the user explicitly quotes them in their own message
* multi-engine architecture stays clean: capabilities are engine-agnostic
  decorators on the prompt, not engine-internal features

Each capability is a small object exposing:

    ``name``:     str — used in logs / traces
    ``enabled`` (bool): True if the user toggled it on for this turn
    ``execute`` (async callable): turns the user message into a
        ``CapabilityResult`` (block text + status metadata)

Capabilities register themselves with :func:`get_capability` for dispatch.

Speech-to-text provider contracts.

ASR is deliberately separate from :mod:`backend.capabilities.tts` and from
the chat capability framework.  It is an input adapter: the caller chooses
when to record, and the resulting text is only returned to the caller.  The
text is not persisted as a chat message or memory until the user explicitly
sends it through the normal chat path.

Image-understanding capability.

User-triggered implicitly (upload an image = you want it understood).
The chat orchestrator runs this in parallel with Call-0a routing and
splices the resulting text descriptions into the *user message*, NOT
the system prompt.

This is the key architectural difference from M1 web_search:

* M1 (web_search): results are reference material → system prompt
* M2 (image understanding): descriptions are what the user sent → user message

Image descriptions deliberately do NOT enter long-term memory (same
philosophy as web search snippets — they are ephemeral by definition).

The capability picks a :class:`VisionProvider` based on
``settings.vision_provider`` and caches it. Provider switch requires a
restart.

Motion generation — hatch-pet paradigm: one sheet per action.

OpenAI hatch-pet 官方工艺（Phase B 复盘后采用）：

    一个动作的所有帧在 **同一张图** 里按网格布局一次生成 ——
    帧间身份/画风一致性由"同图内生"保证，从根上消灭逐帧调用的
    "每帧换人"问题（image-01 逐帧重绘已实测失败：chibi→写实路人）。

    底图（neutral.png）作为身份锚点随每次调用附加；生成条带后由
    sprite_compiler.split_sprite_grid 确定性切帧，再进既有
    色键/稳像/发布管线。

Prompt 契约（全部继承 hatch-pet 的效果纪律）：

- 布局：cols×rows 网格，row-major 摆放 count 个姿态，尾部空格=纯背景
- 身份：与参考图同一角色，画风/脸/服饰/配色/比例完全一致
- 背景：与角色主色冲突最少的纯平色键色，空格也是纯背景
- 禁止：投影/运动线/速度线/文字/网格线/格子边框/分离特效/场景元素
- 状态语义：idle=呼吸微动；wave=仅手臂；jump 类=仅身体位置（无落尘）

OpenAI-compatible GPT Image 2.5 editing adapter for desktop-pet assets.

The desktop application never calls Codex's internal ``$imagegen`` capability.
Instead it uses the public Images Edits API.  Motion requests deliberately
send exactly two immutable inputs in the proven order: canonical identity
(Image 1), then the layout guide (Image 2).  The original upload is retained
in the local run manifest for provenance, not sent as a third visual anchor.

Provider implementations for capabilities (web search, vision, ...).

A provider is a thin async wrapper around one upstream API. Capabilities
pick a provider based on the matching ``settings.*_provider`` field; this
keeps the capability layer ignorant of which API the user pays for.

MiniMax vision-language provider.

Calls the configured VL model (settings.vision_model, default MiniMax-M3)
through the same chat-completions endpoint as the
text client, but with the OpenAI multimodal message format (content as
an array of text + image_url blocks).

Shares the ``MINIMAX_API_KEY`` and ``MINIMAX_BASE_URL`` settings with
the main conversation LLM. No extra API key needed.
DashScope Qwen-Audio non-streaming ASR adapter.

Tavily Search provider — primary backend for the web_search capability.

Tavily is a paid AI-search API with a generous free tier (1k queries /
month at time of writing). It returns ready-to-render snippets instead
of raw HTML, which is what the chat orchestrator wants.

Endpoint reference: https://docs.tavily.com/docs/rest-api/api-reference

We deliberately do NOT use the ``advanced`` search depth by default —
``basic`` is significantly cheaper and the orchestrator already runs an
LLM over the results, so deep retrieval adds latency without much extra
quality. Operators can flip the depth via ``settings``.

TTS (text-to-speech) output capability.

整句 TTS 路径：等 assistant 文本完整后，剥离朗读噪音（动作 []、情绪
token、表情符号），调 minimax T2A V2 API，把 mp3 hex 解码后 base64
包装进 ``TtsAudioResult``。SSE 旁路发 ``event: audio`` 事件给前端。

设计原则：
* 输出型 capability（继承 :class:`OutputCapability`），不进 system prompt
* 失败不阻塞 chat —— 内部 catch，返回 ``status="error"``
* cancellation-safe —— ``asyncio.CancelledError`` 直接 raise 让
  orchestrator 处理（用户切分支时丢弃）
* 复用 minimax_api_key / minimax_base_url 凭证

Web-search capability.

User-triggered (no tool-call). When the user has the 🔍 toggle on, the chat
orchestrator runs this capability in parallel with the rest of the prep
work and splices the result block into the system prompt.

Search results deliberately do NOT enter long-term memory:

* they are ephemeral by definition (the news today is stale next week)
* the orchestrator only ever feeds the rendered ``CapabilityResult.block``
  into the prompt — it never calls ``memory.add_working`` or
  ``memory.episodic.add`` on the raw snippets
* the user's own messages are still recorded normally, so if they want a
  search result remembered they can quote it themselves

The capability picks one of its registered :class:`SearchProvider`
implementations at import time and caches it. Provider switch requires a
restart (intentional — providers carry API keys and connections).

A bounded, read-side compatibility shim for character-card macros.

Imported card text stays verbatim on disk. This module only renders a small,
explicitly documented subset at prompt/display time. Values supplied by the
current user or chat are protected while expansion runs, so macro-looking text
inside user content is never interpreted a second time.

Chinese-aware BM25 ranker for skill chunks.

Replaces the legacy weighted-substring scorer (``_score_module_for_query``)
with proper BM25 + jieba tokenization. Solves the rare-keyword starvation
problem where common terms (the character's name, the setting's name)
dominate over query-specific rare terms (niche factions, rare items).

Each ``ChunkBM25`` instance owns a private ``jieba.Tokenizer()`` seeded
with the proper nouns mined from this skill's chunk metadata
(keywords/title fields). The default jieba dictionary doesn't know
these terms and would split them into single chars that the tokenizer
would then drop entirely, zeroing out their BM25 contribution.
Per-instance tokenizers avoid polluting jieba's process-global dict
across skills.

Cached by content fingerprint: BM25 index is rebuilt only when the
skill modules content actually changes. See ``_content_fingerprint``
for why this is keyed on serialized content rather than ``id()``.

Worldview-agnostic chunk selection for system-prompt injection.

Three layers, in order:

1. ``always=True`` chunks are handled directly by ``PromptBuilder`` and not
   considered here.
2. ``priority_modules`` are returned first when a caller provides them.
   Call-0 module selections flow through this path. They are validated and
   deduped, but not capped by ``top_k``.
3. Optional augmentation can add adjacent list chunks and BM25-ish fallback
   chunks. It is enabled by default; set ``CHUNK_SELECTOR_DISABLE_AUGMENT=1``
   only for comparison testing.

No worldview-specific keywords are coded here.

Per-character chunk vector index.

Embeds skill chunk content with bge-m3 and stores in a dedicated
``chunks_{character}`` ChromaDB collection (separate from episodic
memory). Used by ``chunk_selector`` as the dense-retrieval lane in the
hybrid BM25+vector RRF pipeline.

Index lifecycle: lazy-built on first query for a skill modules dict,
keyed by a content fingerprint (see ``_content_fingerprint`` in
``chunk_bm25``). Two distinct dict objects carrying the same content
share an index, and any change to any meta field invalidates the cache.
The ChromaDB collection itself is persistent — content hash in the
document id de-duplicates across rebuilds.

Failure mode: if embedding API fails, the index is empty; the hybrid
fuser sees an empty vector ranking and falls back to BM25-only. No
exception propagates.
Small image helpers shared across API and service layers.

N-gram repetition diagnostics for assistant outputs.

Computes 4-gram self-overlap between the latest assistant turn and
the previous N assistant turns already in the prompt. The score is
the fraction of 4-grams in the latest turn that also appear in the
prior-turn set — higher means more verbatim reuse of surface phrasing.

This is a *diagnostic* module: it never blocks generation, never
modifies the prompt, never feeds back to the LLM. The score is
recorded in the per-turn trace so authors can see when their skill
file produces an output that is highly templated relative to its own
recent history.

The exact algorithm is the one SillyTavern's Repetition Inspector
uses (n-gram bag intersection). It is intentionally crude: the goal
is a single number in [0, 1] that monotonically tracks "how much of
this reply did I just write". A 4-gram window is large enough that
random overlap is rare (most 4-grams are unique), small enough that
"X 说……X 懂……" type templated phrasing registers.

Why not bigger (5/6-gram)? They undercount real repetition because
a single character change makes the n-gram "new".
Why not smaller (2/3-gram)? They overcount: common Chinese
particles (的/了/是) form a baseline of ~30% that drowns the signal.

Marker-driven markdown skill loader.

Authors can put any markdown files inside the skill folder. The loader
recognises semantic roles via HTML-comment markers (``<!-- name: ... -->``,
``<!-- skill_context -->``, ``<!-- sampling: ... -->``,
``<!-- opening: ... -->``,
``<!-- opening -->`` (block form: the rest of the file is a multi-line
greeting), ``<!-- raw -->`` (skip the meta-narration cleaner — imported
card text must survive verbatim), ``<!-- skip_module -->``,
``<!-- keywords: ... -->``).

If no markers are found, the loader falls back to a small set of legacy
filename hints so existing skills (demo-skill, demo-skill, etc.) keep
loading without any edits. The hints live only in this module — the
hard-coded-lore scanner explicitly allowlists this file as the single
permitted fallback site.

Split large skill modules into retrievable chunks.

Uses ``langchain-text-splitters``:
- ``MarkdownHeaderTextSplitter`` for structural splits on ``#``/``##``/``###``
- ``RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter`` as fallback for oversized sections

Output dict format is the contract with downstream consumers
(``chunk_selector``, ``prompt_builder``, ``knowledge_resolver``,
``skill_router``). All field names are preserved.

Call-0: lightweight routing plus optional skill module selection.

The first LLM call decides whether the turn needs lore and rewrites the query
without seeing any skill module manifest. Only lore turns get a second LLM call
that sees the compressed manifest and selects relevant module IDs.

The prompt below stays worldview-agnostic on purpose: it must work for any
character (fantasy, wuxia, sci-fi, original) without code changes.

SQLite-backed runtime overrides for provider API keys.

Lets the user paste their own MiniMax / DeepSeek key from the UI without
restarting the backend. ``.env`` keeps working as the boot-time default —
the SQLite table is consulted first, and an empty/missing row falls back
to the env value.

We keep this small and self-contained: one table, one connection per call,
no migrations framework. The runtime cost is negligible because each LLM
turn already does network I/O.

Security: the SQLite file lives under ``data/`` next to other character
data. Anyone with filesystem access can read it; that's the same trust
boundary as ``.env``. We never log the key value, and the GET endpoint
only reports presence + timestamp.

Generic OpenAI Chat Completions client for custom chat routes.

Built per request from an immutable ``PrimaryChatConfig`` snapshot — it
never reads ``settings.primary_model`` or the shared client singleton,
so switching ``chat.primary`` can never move the auxiliary callers and
a mid-stream settings change can never mix configurations inside one
running request (ADR 0014).

The public surface is exactly ``BaseLLMClient.stream / complete /
complete_with_tools``; the three legacy clients (MiniMax / DeepSeek /
Ollama) are untouched and remain the inherit-mode path.

Compat profiles concentrate protocol quirks:

* ``minimax``  — strip ``<think>…</think>`` reasoning spans (streaming
  in-band + buffered), matching the validated MiniMax behaviour;
* ``deepseek`` / ``openai`` / ``generic`` — plain Chat Completions.

Only parameters the model declared (or the route baseline) carries are
sent: ``None`` values are filtered, unknown sampling keys never reach
the payload.  Reasoning controls (``reasoning_effort`` / ``thinking``)
are deliberately NOT implemented in V1 — no mapping, no guessing.

chat.primary binding resolution — the per-turn request snapshot.

``resolve_primary_chat_config()`` is the single entry point the chat
orchestrator calls ONCE per turn, before any model I/O:

* returns ``None``  → inherit mode.  The orchestrator keeps using the
  legacy path (shared ``get_llm_client()`` + ``settings.primary_model``)
  byte-for-byte; a user who never enables the new binding sees exactly
  the pre-registry behaviour.
* returns a frozen :class:`PrimaryChatConfig` → custom mode.  The
  orchestrator builds the route client from this snapshot only; global
  settings and the shared singleton are never consulted again this turn,
  so switching the binding mid-stream cannot mix configurations.

Deleting or disabling the bound model/route raises
:class:`PrimaryChatConfigError` — the turn fails with a readable error
BEFORE any provider call.  It never silently falls back to another
(potentially paid) provider.

All reads here are synchronous SQLite (same cost class as the existing
api_key_store lookups); async callers wrap with ``asyncio.to_thread``.

Built-in provider catalog.

Code-only convenience metadata for well-known text-chat providers.  The
catalog is NOT auto-installed: nothing is written to the registry at
startup or import time.  Adding a provider from the catalog is an
explicit user action (``POST /settings/providers {"catalog_id": ...}``)
that creates the account + route rows; models are added by the user
(suggestion list, discovery or manual entry) and never auto-written.

``suggested_models`` are convenience hints for the UI, not claims: each
id is either already used by this project's validated configuration or
is the provider's documented flagship chat id.  Users can add, edit or
ignore them freely.

V1 protocol coverage: ``openai-completions`` routes plus the existing
``ollama-native`` path.  A catalog entry does not mean "every protocol
the vendor offers is supported" — only the protocol written here is.

Provider registry: accounts, routes, model definitions and bindings.

The registry is the storage half of chat-model provider standardization
(ADR 0014).  It intentionally mirrors the ``api_key_store`` pattern:

* tables live in the shared ``data/conversations.db`` and are created on
  first access with ``CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`` — repeatable, no
  migration framework, no startup writes;
* an absent row is a meaningful state: no ``model_bindings`` row for a
  purpose means "inherit the legacy global configuration";
* plaintext credentials are NEVER stored here.  Ordinary rows keep only
  ``credential_ref`` strings; the secret itself lives in the existing
  ``provider_api_keys`` table (SQLite override → ``.env`` fallback) and
  is only ever resolved internally for an outgoing request.

Security invariants pinned by tests:

* no getter in this module returns a key value;
* corrupted JSON columns degrade to empty structures instead of raising;
* deleting an account/model that ``chat.primary`` still references is
  refused instead of silently rebinding to another provider.

Shared LLM client singleton. Import ``get_llm_client`` instead of calling
``create_llm_client()`` at module level.

Single language slot (ADR 0015): ``model_bindings(purpose="chat.primary")``
is the single source of truth for ALL text generation.  The legacy
``settings.llm_provider`` / ``settings.primary_model`` (and the minimax /
ollama model fields) are derived caches written through on every binding
save; ``get_llm_client()`` is slot-aware so every auxiliary caller that
uses the singleton follows the same slot with zero per-caller changes.
Safe parsing helpers for structured tool-call arguments.
Bounded OpenAI tool-stream assembly; never yields incomplete arguments.

Per-turn LLM call tracer for postmortem debugging.

Writes one JSONL file per turn under ``data/debug/{character}_{conversation_id}/turn_NNN.jsonl``,
with one line per call (call0_router / call1_chat / call2_extract).

Disable via ``DEBUG_TRACE_ENABLED=false``.  Trace files are never cleaned
automatically (ADR 0027): users clear them from Settings → 数据管理, per
character or globally.  Chat and memory data live outside ``data/debug/``
and are untouched by that deletion.

SiliconFlow embedding client (OpenAI-compatible API).

Replaces sentence-transformers local model with API calls to bge-m3.

Branch-scoped persona mode (`relaxed` vs `strict`).

`relaxed` is the historical default — the role can answer tool-flavoured
requests (出题/写代码/翻译/解题) using the base LLM's general capability,
which works well for utility users but leaks abilities the character
shouldn't have. `strict` adds a hard prompt clause telling the model to
reject or transform tool requests in-character, preserving immersion for
roleplay-first users.

Mode is stored at ``branches[*].meta.persona_mode`` so users can pick a
different stance per conversation. Default stays ``relaxed`` so existing
branches see no behavioural change.
Stable Chroma collection names for character/branch vector memory.

Small, dependency-free request observability helpers.

The desktop app is local-first, so this intentionally keeps metrics in memory

Persistent local recordings and orchestration for speech-to-text.

The service owns the recording lifecycle, while provider-specific HTTP lives
in ``backend.capabilities.providers``.  A recording is written before the
remote call starts, so a provider failure never loses the source audio and a
later retry never needs to upload it again.

GPT Image 2.5 strip generation via the proven two-image Codex recipe
(identity baseline, then layout guide).  The former H3 (ComfyUI) and
manual-import providers were removed on 2026-09-03; `get_provider("gpt-image-2")`

Bounded-retry filesystem primitives for staging-style directory swaps
and durable JSON writes.

On Windows, antivirus/indexer processes can hold a freshly written
file or directory for a moment; the first ``Path.rename``/``os.replace``
then fails with ``PermissionError`` even though the application itself
keeps no handle.  Affected flows (pack publish, image-pack promotion,
portrait staging, ``run.json`` / ``job.json`` / ``candidate.json`` /
``pet_works.json`` / retention-state writes) all rename a temp file
into its final name, so the retry and unique-temp pattern live here
once instead of per service.
Bootstrap immutable packaged skills into the user's writable skill root.

Portable v2 ZIP archives for character data.

The archive deliberately stores logical memory records instead of database or
Chroma implementation details, so a backup made before a storage migration can
be restored after it.
Short-lived proof that a destructive import was preceded by an export.

SillyTavern-style character card import (TavernAI V1 / CCv2 / CCv3).

A character card is one JSON document; PNG / JSON / CHARX are just
containers (the PNG carries the JSON base64-encoded in a tEXt chunk).
Parsing normalizes all three spec generations into a single CardData
shape and the converter emits a flat markdown skill folder — the same
target format as manual uploads, so the loader, routing and prompt
builder need zero card-specific knowledge.

Design contract (docs/tasks/character_card_import_research.md):
- Card text is imported VERBATIM: macros stay (rendered at read time by
  ``backend.core.card_macros``), and every ``<!--`` inside card content is
  neutralized to ``<\!--`` (idempotent) so imported text can never forge
  loader markers. Generated files also carry ``<!-- raw -->`` so the
  loader skips its legacy meta-narration cleaner.
- The card is untrusted input: container size caps, book-entry caps,

Base URL: ``https://ilinkai.weixin.qq.com``  (6 endpoints)

* ``GET  /ilink/bot/get_bot_qrcode``  → returns ``{qrcode, qrcode_img_content, ret}``
* ``GET  /ilink/bot/get_qrcode_status?qrcode=...``  → returns

* ``POST /ilink/bot/getupdates``  → long polling, 35s server hold.
  Body: ``{get_updates_buf: "...", base_info: {channel_version: "..."}}``.
  Response: ``{ret, msgs: [...], get_updates_buf: "..."}``. Each msg:
  ``{from_user_id, to_user_id, client_id, message_type, message_state,
  item_list: [{type, text_item/voice_item/image_item/...}], context_token}``.
* ``POST /ilink/bot/sendmessage``  → outbound. Body shape:
  ``{base_info, msg: {from_user_id: "", to_user_id, client_id,
  message_type: 2 (BOT), message_state: 2 (FINISH), item_list: [...],
  context_token}}``. ``message_type=2`` means BOT-side, MUST be set.
  Echoes the most recent ``context_token`` from the inbound message.
* ``POST /ilink/bot/getuploadurl``  → pre-signed CDN URL for media upload
  (AES-128-ECB encrypted). Required for image/voice/file/video send.
* ``POST /ilink/bot/getconfig`` and ``POST /ilink/bot/sendtyping``  →
  used for the "正在输入…" indicator (Phase 4.1).

All requests carry the headers:
    AuthorizationType: ilink_bot_token
    Authorization:    Bearer <bot_token>
    X-WECHAT-UIN:     base64(<random uint32>)
    Content-Length:   <byte length of body utf-8>   (upstream sets this
                     explicitly; httpx computes it automatically for json=,
                     but we keep the convention noted for reference)

Image / voice / file / video outbound is non-trivial: it requires uploading
the encrypted bytes to a CDN first (via getuploadurl + AES-128-ECB on the
client side, then PUT to CDN), then referencing the resulting CDNMedia

For the MVP text + "image as URL" path we use a shortcut: many iLink
clients treat ``image_url`` as a hint for outbound images if the protocol

- RECLAIMABLE  provably unreferenced by anything, past the 1-hour

- UNKNOWN      safety cannot be proven: unreadable index/database,

Step 4-6 (桌宠融合): pet policy package.

PetPolicy owns the decision loop ("did the AI ask the pet to do
something?"). The **ServerCommandValidator** then turns that intent
into validated PetCommand rows in the SQLite command bus. The bus
itself uses three command types (state / transient / exec) and a
three-state ACK lifecycle (pending → delivered → accepted →
completed / failed / expired). **PetPolicy does NOT generate dialogue
text** — it only decides presentation of an existing message_id.

Public surface:
- ``policy.PetPolicy``                 (Step 6 wires LLM)
- ``policy.get_pet_policy``            (singleton accessor)
- ``policy.set_pet_policy``            (for tests + wiring)
- ``validator.ServerCommandValidator``  (Step 4)
- ``bus.PetCommandBus``                (Step 4)
- ``snapshot.PetPresenceSnapshot``     (Step 4)
- ``store.init_pet_tables``            (Step 4)
- ``tools.DECIDE_PRESENTATION_TOOL``   (Step 6)

This package is intentionally backend-only — the Electron host reads
the snapshot via /pet/state and pulls commands via /pet/outbox.

Step 4 — SQLite-backed PetCommandBus.

State machine:
    pending → delivered → accepted → completed (happy path)
                            ├→ failed (exec failed at Electron side)
                  └→ expired (TTL elapsed before accept)

Restart rules (this is the critical bit):
- state commands:  restartable. PetApp on startup pulls all latest
                   ``state`` rows and applies them — no replay of
                   voice / move.
- transient commands: NOT replayed. If PetApp restarts, transient
                   rows are wasted; the host re-emits if needed.
- exec commands: NOT replayed unless the client already ACK'd them
                   (i.e. accepted). Server keeps ``accepted`` rows
                   for the duration of their TTL so a network blip
                   mid-execution doesn't silently lose the result.

Concurrency: per-(character, branch) writers may step on each other
(validator writes, policy writes). The contract says each row's
``id`` is monotonic per (character, branch) — clients rely on that
for cursor advancement. SQLite ``AUTOINCREMENT`` + ``IMMEDIATE`` tx
gives us the monotonic guarantee. We do NOT add per-(character,
branch) locking here; the (character, branch, id) index is the read
synchronization point.

Step 6 (桌宠融合): PetPolicy — embodied presentation decision loop.

PetPolicy does NOT generate dialogue text. It only decides how an
already-existing message (identified by message_id) should be embodied
on the desktop pet: mood, gesture, bubble, and voice. Physical locomotion
remains a runtime-owned event; the locomotion field is retained only as a
semantic intent for the host and is not started by policy.

Architecture (four layers):
  1. ChatOrchestrator          → generates text (SOLE source)
  2. PetPolicy (this module)   → decides presentation  ← Step 6
  3. ServerCommandValidator    → validates intent       ← Step 4
  4. PetCommandBus             → persists commands     ← Step 4

Event flow:
  notify_*() event hooks
        ↓
  per-(character,branch) asyncio.Queue
        ↓
  per-(character,branch) queue + cooldown check
        ↓
  LLM: complete_with_tools([decide_presentation_tool])
        ↓
  0 tool_calls → ignore (no-op)
  1 tool_call  → parse → ServerCommandValidator.validate()
                    → PetCommandBus.issue()
                    → result published via SSE /pet/outbox
  failure      → ignore + log trace

事件策略：消息呈现事件不合并、不冷却；emotion_change 走代码路径，
session_switch 不调用模型；其余消息事件按队列顺序处理。
消息事件有 message_id 时永远不能被无消息状态事件覆盖；同一 turn_id 只呈现一次。

Step 4 — PetPresenceSnapshot (read-only view).

The Electron host owns the authoritative runtime actor state. This
snapshot is the **service-side expectation**, used by PetApp /pet/state
to render something useful on first paint after a restart. Updates
flow through ``bus.update_presence(...)`` whenever a ``state`` command
is issued; client observed_state feedback (Step 6 wires it) lands in
``last_observed_at_ms``.

Step 4 — pet_commands + pet_presence SQLite tables.

We share ``conversations.db`` (already used by ``working_memory``) so
the pet's history lives next to the character's chat history. Two
tables:

- ``pet_commands`` — append-only queue with state machine
  (pending → delivered → accepted → completed | failed | expired).
  Three command classes: ``state`` (latest-only, persists),
  ``transient`` (TTL-based, expired if not consumed in time),
  ``exec`` (single-shot, needs command_id idempotency + completion
  callback).
- ``pet_presence`` — service-side "expected state". NOT the actual
  state; the Electron host owns the real state in its runtime actor. We keep
  this so PetApp /pet/state has something to render after a restart.

Schema choices worth noting:
- ``id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT`` gives a monotonic per-(character,
  branch) seq the client uses as cursor. command_id is a separate UUID
  for client-side idempotency.
- We don't put x/y in payload — those are computed by the Electron
  host from semantic intents (wander / near_cursor / edge / home).
- Status transitions are append-only on the same row — UPDATE pet_commands
  SET status = ... WHERE id = ?. No DELETE except cleanup_expired().

Step 6 (桌宠融合): ``decide_presentation`` tool schema.

PetPolicy owns this tool — it is NOT part of the character's Skill
schema and is never exposed to the memory-extraction / consolidation
pipeline. The LLM must call this tool to express how an already-existing
message (identified by message_id) should be embodied on the desktop pet.

**PetPolicy does NOT generate dialogue text.** It only decides presentation
of an existing message. The ChatOrchestrator is the sole source of text.

Step 4 — ServerCommandValidator (pure function).

Takes a ``decide_presentation`` intent (output of PetPolicy / mock
LLM in Step 5 / Step 6) and validates it against the schema + the
running character's working memory. Emits zero or more
``PetCommand`` issues. **Coordinates (x/y) are NEVER produced here** —
the Electron host is the only process that reads ``screen`` and
resolves semantic intents (``wander`` / ``near_cursor`` / ``edge``
/ ``home``) to real pixels.

Validation rules:
1. Each intent field is clamped to its enum.
2. ``presentation.message_id`` must reference a real working_memory
   row (user or assistant). If the message doesn't exist or has been
   aged out, the validator downgrades to ``attention=ignore``.
3. ``voice=existing_audio`` but ``audio_url`` is empty → degrade to
   ``voice=none`` (PetPolicy shouldn't promise playback if there's no
   audio URL).
4. Same message_id can't produce a bubble within 5 s — we keep an
   in-process LRU keyed on ``(character, branch_id, message_id)`` for
   5 s.
5. ``locomotion`` is one of the semantic intents — never x/y. We
   store that as-is only when the caller explicitly allows it; the normal
   PetPolicy path disables it because physical movement is runtime-owned.

Output:
- Calls ``bus.issue(...)`` zero or more times (one PetCommand per
  visible action). State commands dedupe on ``(kind)`` so the latest
  ``set_mood`` wins.
- Calls ``bus.update_presence(...)`` to reflect the latest expected
  state.

Proactive outreach engine — content-driven check-ins + silence fallback.

Two trigger families feed the same durable ledger (``wx_trigger_store``):

1. ``check_in`` (primary, content-driven): after each user-initiated turn,
   ``run_proactive_schedule`` lets the character decide whether the *content*
   of that conversation warrants a follow-up ("她下周要考试 → 明早关心一下"),
   and schedules a future trigger at the character-chosen time.
2. ``silence`` / ``silence_probe`` (fallback): when the user has been quiet,
   a probe runs a cheap deterministic gate (L1), then an LLM judgment call
   (L2) asking the character whether it would naturally reach out now. The
   verdict may also reschedule the next probe ("判完设 timer"), which is the
   same future-due-trigger mechanism an agent's commitment timer would use.

The engine loop is channel-agnostic: it leases due triggers and routes them
to a ``TriggerSource`` by ``kind``. When a trigger fires, ``ProactiveEngine.fire``
generates the message through the *normal* chat pipeline
(``run_chat_for_wx`` with ``origin="proactive"``, ``persist_user_input=False``,
``schedule_memory_extraction=False``) and hands the result to a publisher
(the app SSE channel in ``api/chat.py``; WeChat is a later leg).

Video frame extraction and sprite sheet compilation pipeline.

Expects a directory of RGBA PNG frames (the compiled output of
``split_sprite_grid``, or user upload). Uses only PIL (Pillow) and the
standard library — no ffmpeg dependency.

Pipeline (compile_pack):

    frames_dir → unified background estimation → chroma-key each frame
    against that ONE shared colour → optional stabilisation on the original
    cell canvas → union-bbox crop → numbered PNG frames
    (the source of truth) + sprite sheet (render optimisation) + a
    PetPack-v2 clip fragment ready to merge into a manifest.

Stabilisation semantics (2026-08 批次2-C2):

- ``none``       — leave every frame as-is.
- ``feet``       — align each frame's foot anchor (centroid-x of the
                   bottom-most non-transparent alpha row). Vertical
                   displacement is preserved, so jumps/approaches keep
                   their real motion; only ground jitter is removed.
- ``grounded``   — force all frames of an in-place loop onto one foot line.
- ``horizontal`` — correct horizontal camera shake only.

The old centre-of-mass alignment was deliberately removed: it pulled
real vertical action back into place and made animations look like
in-place trembling.

Durable proactive-trigger ledger (SQLite).

The proactive engine (``proactive.py``) drives *all* proactive outreach
through this store. Every trigger is a persisted row with a ``due_at_ms``;
the scheduler leases rows that are due, routes them to a ``TriggerSource``
by ``kind``, and marks them fired/cancelled.

Why durable + due-at rather than an in-memory timer: this is the same shape
as the qixing agent's ``scheduled_triggers`` table, so a future agent can
schedule timers/commitments by inserting rows with a future ``due_at_ms``
and the existing scheduler loop fires them with zero changes. "Silence"
today is just a source that schedules probe triggers; agent timers are a
new source, not a new mechanism.

Schema
------
proactive_triggers(
    trigger_id     TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    kind           TEXT NOT NULL,        -- "check_in" | "silence_probe" | "silence" | (future: "timer", ...)
    character      TEXT NOT NULL,
    branch_id      TEXT NOT NULL,
    due_at_ms      INTEGER NOT NULL,     -- epoch ms; scheduler leases when now >= due
    status         TEXT NOT NULL,        -- pending | leased | fired | cancelled
    lease_until_ms INTEGER NOT NULL,     -- concurrency lease: another worker must not touch until this
    attempts       INTEGER NOT NULL,
    payload_json   TEXT NOT NULL,        -- source-specific context (topic/reason/…)
    created_at_ms  INTEGER NOT NULL,
    fired_at_ms    INTEGER
)

Deterministic A-E condition transforms over frozen Call-1 fixtures.

Plan section 6. Every transform edits section-level content of the frozen
fixture (never regex over the giant prompt): targets are located by
exact-match against captured sections and every edit is loud — if a
target cannot be located unambiguously the transform raises instead of
silently producing a wrong ablation.

- A Baseline        : identity (byte-exact reconstruction, test-pinned).
- B No Anti-Template: drop ONLY the anti-template writing-metadata hint
                      from the user turn; emotion hint and the whole
                      system prompt untouched.
- C Relationship State Only: drop ONLY the "- 回应倾向：" response
                      guidance line from the relationship prompt part;
                      every state line (stage, quality bands, trends,
                      impression, inside jokes, milestones, narrative)
                      survives byte-exactly.
- D Protocol-Only Boundary: rebuild the final response boundary keeping
                      hard contracts (fact priority, no-fabrication,
                      bracket output protocol, stage fact, markdown ban)
                      and dropping soft choreography (length rules,
                      action-dosage prescription, WeChat-style bubble
                      segmentation).
- E Character Native: B + C + D composed.

Round 2 (task doc section 4, minimal production config A/B/F/G):

- F = B + C composed (drop_anti_template + relationship_state_only).
- G = F + minimal_assistant_boundary: the boundary's soft conversational
  choreography is dropped with the same line predicates as D (protocol
  content survives byte-exactly) and the fixed Minimal Boundary text from
  task doc §4.1 is appended VERBATIM — implementers are not allowed to
  reword a single character (pinned by tests and by the constant below).

Round 3 (task doc section 5, example authority & history style
contamination; G is the validated baseline and becomes the control):

- G0 = the existing G transform under the round-3 label (control).
- E1 = G0 + move_examples_near_generation: the examples part is
  REORDERED to sit after all runtime context and immediately before the
  roleplay anchor / protocol boundary cluster. Content is byte-identical
  (same single part string, same prompt_sections text); no "please
  imitate" instruction is ever added — §5.3 measures natural ICL
  position weight only. If a fixture has no examples part (e.g. real
  cards whose loader yields none) the move is a recorded no-op.
- H1 = G0 + reduced assistant history: every user turn survives; only
  the LAST 2 assistant turns stay in the messages history in full form;
  OLDER assistant turns are removed entirely (never converted into user
  turns — §5.4). ``history_messages`` is legitimately rewritten for
  H1/EH1, so the shared invariant checker swaps the frozen-history pin
  for the dedicated §5.4 invariants on those conditions.
- EH1 = E1 + H1 composed.

Round 4 (task doc section 6, Character Reaction Sketch; G stays the
validated baseline and R0 relabels it as the round-4 control):

- R0 = the G transform under the round-4 label (direct generation, no
  planner call, no injection).
- R1 = R0 + a NEUTRAL reaction sketch (same-cost planner call that sees
  NO character information) injected as ephemeral runtime state.
- R2 = R0 + a CHARACTER reaction sketch injected the same way.

Three LLM-judge task types over a round-4 run, all manual-eval gated
(``--apply`` performs real provider calls) and all blind to the
condition where seeing it would bias the verdict:

- ``behavior``  — Behavior Appropriateness (1-5, THE core new metric):
  "would THIS character, in THIS relationship stage and situation,
  naturally take this interactive behaviour" — cold answering 别问了 with
  好。 = 5; answering with gentle assistant care = 1-2. Scored for every
  ok row (R0/R1/R2 alike), canon + stage + user message + reply only.
- ``follow``    — Reaction Follow Rate (0-2 per sketch field): does the
  reply follow the injected sketch's stance / impulse / restraint /
  initiative? restraint_follow is the headline metric — the easiest
  place for the base model's prior to override the character's decision
  (§6.7 d). Only R1/R2 rows with a sketch.
- ``identity``  — Sketch Role Specificity: given ONLY a sketch and the
  four character canons (labels A-D, deterministically shuffled per
  sample), the judge guesses which character it describes. Random
  baseline is 25%; R1's sketches should sit AT the baseline (they carry
  no persona) which validates the control, while R2 below ~baseline
  means the planner just re-emits "understand the user" (§6.7 a).
  ``_identity_options`` also returns the correct label so the metrics
  layer can score guesses WITHOUT re-deriving the canon→label mapping
  (a text-equality trap: blocks map label→canon text, not label→name).

Unlike judge_llm (rounds 1-3), payloads carry the real user message and

The sketch is a separate, independent LLM call made at REPLAY time, before
Call-1 (§6.2-§6.5): tiny fixed JSON schema, low temperature, 100-150 max
tokens, never a reply draft. Its output is ephemeral runtime state —
injected into the system prompt between the roleplay anchor and the
protocol boundary, never written into any history, memory or relationship
layer, discarded at the end of the turn.

Conditions (§6.3):
- R0 Direct                : G baseline, no planner call, no injection.
- R1 Neutral Sketch Control: same-cost planner call with NO character
  information — it may only analyse the interaction itself (user message,
  relationship stage line, dialogue turn count). This controls the "one
  extra deliberation step / a bit more context" effect and is NOT a
  production candidate.
- R2 Character Sketch      : planner sees the character's identity and
  personality, relationship factual state, emotion state, memory facts,
  minimal recent context and the current user message.

Prompt discipline (§6.4): the planner never sees the Final Response
Boundary, the Anti-Template hint, response-style instructions, or large
assistant history, and the prompt never says "don't sound like an AI".
R1 additionally must not see the character name, skill context, examples,
core memory or assistant turns (any of those would leak persona into the
control).

The output schema is IDENTICAL for R1 and R2 so every planner metric
(§6.7 follow rate, identity, cross-character distance) applies to both —
the only difference is whether the persona is visible to the planner.
Forbidden keys (should_ask_question / should_comfort / response_length /
should_end_conversation / response_structure) are rejected: any of them
would smuggle a new hidden chat template back into the pipeline (§6.2).

All conditions stream from the SAME frozen fixture with identical model /
provider / sampling / max_tokens / history; only the ablation transform

Concurrency (user requirement 2026-09-11): real runs execute with at most
``--concurrency`` (default 2) in-flight Call-1 requests. Results are

(condition x character x case) N times; the full task list — every
(condition, character, case, replicate) tuple — is shuffled with a fixed

Round-5 N-best reranker — SELECTION ONLY (task doc §7.5-§7.10).

The reranker sees, per pool: character canon, relationship factual
state, memory facts, minimal recent context, the user message and the
pool's candidate replies under shuffled display labels. It never sees
the context condition (G0/EH1), original candidate indexes, judge
scores or anything else about the experiment. It picks; it NEVER
rewrites, merges or extends a candidate (§7.5).

Two independent tasks (§7.19): ``n3`` ranks all three candidates;
``n2`` re-ranks ONLY the first two as a separate pairwise call — the N2
winner is never derived from the N3 ranking, because a three-candidate
field can change a pairwise comparison.

Prompt discipline (§7.7/§7.8): priority order fidelity > behavior
appropriateness > natural character dialogue > continuity/correctness >
assistant discourse (only when it conflicts with the character), with
the length/question/care shortcuts EXPLICITLY forbidden so the selector
cannot flatten every character into terse anti-AI style.

Candidate order is shuffled per (pool, task) with a recorded
display→original mapping (§7.15) so winner-distribution analysis can
detect position bias. Output parsing rejects anything but a full
permutation of the display labels.

Real calls are manual-eval gated: default is --dry-run, ``--apply``
performs provider calls (user-authorized manual eval only).

assistant history) is byte-identical to G0 there and the §5.8 Hypothesis H
has no surface.  This tool generates one 4-turn conversation per character
by replaying the production Call-1 path (G-condition assembly: full
boundary, anti-template hint, user-turn composition) with the fixed user
script from the long-conversation plan (§24, first four turns) — real

The output ``seed_history.json`` is consumed by ``capture.py --seed-history``

Round-5 derived conditions and selection metrics (task doc §7.11-§7.16).

Everything here is OFFLINE derivation over stored artifacts — no model
calls:

- candidate_pools.json (nbest.py)   : pools of independent candidates
- rerank_results.json (reranker.py) : blind shuffled selections (n2/n3)
- llm_judge_r5.json (judge_candidates.py) : per-CANDIDATE final scores

Derived conditions (fully paired, §7.2/§7.3): N1 = candidate 1;
N2 = rerank(c1,c2) winner; N3 = rerank(c1,c2,c3) winner; Random-N3 = a

Tests for ``ILinkBot._login_loop`` probe-retry + selective wipe.

Background
----------
Before this fix, ``_login_loop`` did this when ``_probe_saved_token``
timed out (3s was too aggressive against the iLink cold-start latency):

    logger.warning("probe: network error; entering poll loop optimistically")
    self.connected = True
    self._start_poll_and_dispatch()
    return

That hid a critical failure mode: the bot silently entered poll loop
with an unverified token, the UI showed ``已连接``, but the saved token
might be stale (server changed, session expired, etc.). The QR card
was hidden, so the user had no way to bind the owner — exactly the
"都不给我扫码的机会" complaint.

The first fix (3s → retry 15s → wipe-on-fail) addressed that, but
introduced a new bug: any transient network blip (ReadTimeout that
never reached the server) wiped the persisted token and forced a QR
re-scan on every flaky start. The user saw this as "每次进去都要
重写绑定微信啊" because the new bot identity after re-scan didn't
match the old one — even though ``wx_owner.json`` was unchanged,
the iLink-side bot state was new, so the user had to re-scan and
re-engage with the bot.

The current fix:
* On probe ReadTimeout / ConnectError: retry once with 15s.
* If retry also times out: clear in-memory handles, fall through to
  ``_do_login()`` for a fresh QR, but PRESERVE the persisted token so
  the next start() can re-probe (network is usually back by then).
* On probe 401 / non-2xx (server-side rejection): still wipe — that
  token is provably dead.

Tests below cover the retry-on-network-error, the preserve-on-
double-timeout, the 401 wipe, and the timeout-parameter shape of
``_probe_saved_token``.

Tests for ILinkBot QR auto-refresh on expiry + /wx/refresh_qr endpoint.

Background
----------
Before this fix, ``_do_login`` returned as soon as the iLink server
reported ``status: "expired"``. The bot would then sit idle with a
stale ``qrcode_url`` set, and the UI would keep showing the expired
QR with no way to recover — the user had to disable + enable the
bot to get a fresh QR.

The fix wraps ``_do_login`` in a refresh loop and extracts the
single-QR polling into ``_poll_qr_once``. When a QR expires, the
outer loop fetches a fresh one (up to 20 times, ~100 minutes of
continuous scan window). The user no longer needs to take any
action when their QR expires — they can leave the bot in "waiting
for scan" state indefinitely.

This file covers:
- ``_poll_qr_once`` returns False on token, True on expiry
- ``_do_login`` auto-refreshes on QR expiry (fetches a new one)
- ``_do_login`` exits when ``_stop_event`` is set mid-refresh
- ``/wx/refresh_qr`` endpoint stops + wipes + starts a fresh bot

symbols.name: execute
symbols.docstring:
Describe *images* and return one ``CapabilityResult`` per image.

*vision_need* is the focus hint produced by Call-0-image — a
short string saying "to answer the user, the VL model should
look for X in the image" (e.g. "identify the person", "name
the fruit", "transcribe the visible text"). It is NOT the
user's question and NOT a refined query — the VL model still
cannot resolve pronouns or look up lore, it just looks at the
image with a focus. Empty string ⇒ fall back to a neutral
full description.

image. The data URI sent to the vision API must match the
real format — sending a PNG as ``image/jpeg`` silently
returns an empty description. If *mimes* is missing or
shorter than *images*, the provider falls back to JPEG.

Each image is processed independently — one failure does not
block the others. The caller is responsible for assembling the
results however it wants.

symbols.docstring:
Character import: rebuild branches, chat history, memory_store and vectors.

Design choices:
- **Physical branch collections.** Vector rows are re-embedded when the
  configured embedder is available and written to the imported branch's
  physical Chroma collection.  Older Markdown bundles remain importable, but
  they are normalized to the same branch layout and never recreate the

  silently producing an incomplete restore.

  re-inserted with explicit ``id`` so ``forked_from_message_id`` in
  ``conversation_branches`` keeps pointing at the right turn.

  returns 409 unless the caller explicitly opts into wiping.
- **Skill files: write only when the local skill is missing.** Never
  overwrite an existing local skill — the user's local edits win.
- **Atomic-ish.** SQLite work happens in a single transaction;
  memory_store JSON is written via the store's atomic-rename helper;
  the runtime cache is cleared at the end so the next request reloads
  from disk.

symbols.name: mutate_run
symbols.header: def mutate_run(run_id: str, mutator: Callable[[dict[str, Any]], dict[str, Any] | None]) -> dict[str, Any]:
symbols.docstring:
Serialize one read → transition → save cycle for a generation run.

Every durable run mutation must go through this primitive.  The per-run
lock is shared with the generation workers, so a user action (review /
batch accept / cancel / retry) can never interleave with a worker's
read-modify-write cycle and overwrite freshly generated state with a
stale snapshot (lost update).

A ``threading.Lock`` — not ``asyncio.Lock`` — is deliberate: the guarded
sections are short synchronous file IO (no ``await``), while callers span
the event loop (API endpoints, worker coroutines), ``asyncio.to_thread``
workers and the plain worker threads inside ``pet_works``.  One lock
serializes them all without binding to a specific event loop.

The mutator runs while the lock is held: it may raise (nothing is
persisted) and may return an ``extra`` dict (e.g. ``{"skipped": [...]}``)
that is merged into the fresh public projection this function returns.

symbols.header: """Step 6 (桌宠融合): PetPolicy — embodied presentation decision loop.
symbols.docstring:
Step 6 (桌宠融合): PetPolicy — embodied presentation decision loop.

PetPolicy does NOT generate dialogue text. It only decides how an
already-existing message (identified by message_id) should be embodied
on the desktop pet: mood, gesture, bubble, and voice. Physical locomotion
remains a runtime-owned event; the locomotion field is retained only as a
semantic intent for the host and is not started by policy.

Architecture (four layers):
  1. ChatOrchestrator          → generates text (SOLE source)
  2. PetPolicy (this module)   → decides presentation  ← Step 6
  3. ServerCommandValidator    → validates intent       ← Step 4
  4. PetCommandBus             → persists commands     ← Step 4

Event flow:
  notify_*() event hooks
        ↓
  per-(character,branch) asyncio.Queue
        ↓
  per-(character,branch) queue + cooldown check
        ↓
  LLM: complete_with_tools([decide_presentation_tool])
        ↓
  0 tool_calls → ignore (no-op)
  1 tool_call  → parse → ServerCommandValidator.validate()
                    → PetCommandBus.issue()
                    → result published via SSE /pet/outbox
  failure      → ignore + log trace

事件策略：消息呈现事件不合并、不冷却；emotion_change 走代码路径，
session_switch 不调用模型；其余消息事件按队列顺序处理。
消息事件有 message_id 时永远不能被无消息状态事件覆盖；同一 turn_id 只呈现一次。

PyInstaller entry point for the packaged Windows distribution.

Use this only when building with ``ai-companion.spec``. In development

symbols.name: test_ilink_bot_dispatch
symbols.docstring:
Tests for ``ILinkBot`` message dispatch + serial queue.

Covers (post single-user collapse):
- First message binds the openid as owner
- Subsequent messages from a non-owner openid are silently dropped
  (no welcome, no command/text dispatch, no outbound calls)
- Owner messages reach the command / text handlers
- Welcome message fires exactly once across many owner messages
- Serial dispatch queue preserves arrival order even when each
  handler awaits a long-running operation
- ``rebindWxOwner`` flow: clear → next inbound rebinds

The bot's ``_send_post`` and the per-handler calls are mocked so the
tests run without any network I/O. The bot instance is constructed
without ``start()`` so the real long-poll loop never spins up.
